parameters.name: dates
parameters.description: A column of dates from a marked date table.
parameters.examNote: The date table must be continuous with no gaps and must be marked as a date table in the model.

parameters.name: number_of_intervals
parameters.description: Number of intervals to shift. Use negative numbers to go backward in time.
parameters.examNote: Use -1 for the previous period. Use -12 for 12 months ago. Positive values shift forward.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: The unit of time to shift by.
parameters.examNote: YEAR is most common for year-over-year comparisons. MONTH for month-over-month.

returnType: Table (a set of dates shifted by the specified interval)
summary: DATEADD shifts a set of dates forward or backward by a specified interval. Used inside CALCULATE to compute period-over-period comparisons such as previous year sales, previous quarter revenue, or trailing 12 months.

examples.label: Sales same period last year
examples.explanation: DATEADD shifts the current date filter back by 1 year. If the visual shows Jan 2024, CALCULATE evaluates SUM(Sales[Amount]) for Jan 2023.

steps: Current filter context contains a date range (e.g., Jan 2024 from a year slicer)
DATEADD shifts the entire date range back by 1 YEAR → Jan 2023
CALCULATE replaces the date filter with this shifted set
SUM is evaluated against the prior period's data

commonTraps: Requires a continuous date table explicitly marked as a date table — gaps in dates cause incorrect results.
DATEADD shifts the exact date selection forward or backward. For a full prior calendar year use PREVIOUSYEAR() instead.
SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is shorthand for DATEADD(dates, -1, YEAR) and produces identical results — interchangeable on the exam.
